ruling_text: Seven things invalidate wudhu: urinating; defecating; passing wind from the anus; sleeping such that one's eyes do not see and ears do not hear; things that cause one to lose his mind such as insanity, intoxication, and unconsciousness; istihadah of a woman; janabah, and based on recommended precaution, all things for which one must perform ghusl.
citation_label: Islamic Laws, Things that invalidate wudhu, ruling 322

ruling_text: Near the time of the morning call to prayer, a whiteness in the sky moves upwards from the east; this is known as the first dawn. When this whiteness spreads, it is called the second dawn, which is the start of the prescribed time for the morning prayer. The end of the time for the morning prayer is when the sun rises.
chapter_title: The time for the morning prayer
citation_label: Islamic Laws, The time for the morning prayer, ruling 728

ruling_text: If a fasting person travels after zuhr, he must, based on obligatory precaution, complete his fast and it is not necessary for him to make up that fast. If he travels before zuhr, then based on obligatory precaution, he cannot fast on that day, particularly if he had made the intention to travel the night before.
chapter_title: Rulings of fasting for a traveller
citation_label: Islamic Laws, Rulings of fasting for a traveller, ruling 1690

ruling_text: The Friday prayer is an optional obligation, meaning that on Fridays someone who is duty-bound has the option to either perform the Friday prayer, if all its conditions are fulfilled, or the zuhr prayer; and if he performs the Friday prayer, it will suffice in place of the zuhr prayer.
chapter_title: The Friday prayer and its laws
citation_label: Islamic Laws, The Friday prayer and its laws, ruling 719

ruling_text: The shari criterion with respect to the time of praying and fasting is true fajr, and its determination is the task of the mukallaf.
citation_label: Practical Laws of Islam, Prayer times, Q350

ruling_text: Even though Friday prayer is considered an alternative obligation during this period of time and it is not considered obligatory for people to participate in it, one should not deprive oneself of the blessings gained through attending the prayer solely due to doubt about the justice of the imam or due to irrelevant excuses.
citation_label: Practical Laws of Islam, Friday Prayers, Q602

question_text: If I planned to reach my residence before noon while traveling but did not arrive in time, is my fast valid?
ruling_text: If a fasting person planned to reach his place of residence before noon but did not reach it in time, his fast is invalid while traveling and it is only obligatory for him to perform the qada of fasting for the day in which he did not reach his place of residency; he does not have to pay kaffarah.
citation_label: Practical Laws of Islam, Fasting, Q734

subtopic: Prayer where forbidden music is played
question_text: Can I pray in a place where forbidden music is played?
ruling_text: If being in a place where forbidden music is played entails listening to a haram kind of music, staying there is not permissible, although performing prayer is considered valid. If the sound of music distracts one's attention and concentration, performing prayer there will be makruh.
section_title: Prayer where forbidden music is played
citation_label: Practical Laws of Islam, Prayer, Q383

ruling_text: There are seven things that invalidate wudhu: the discharge of urine; the discharge of faeces; the emission of wind from the anus; falling asleep if sight and hearing are overcome; a state in which the mind is undermined, such as intoxication, insanity, or unconsciousness; istihadah; and any condition that necessitates ghusl, such as janabah.
citation_label: Islamic Law, Taharah, Things that invalidate wudhu, p. 72

ruling_text: When brightness begins to appear in the horizon from the eastern direction that moves vertically, this is the First Fajr or False Fajr, and the morning prayer is not valid at this time. When the brightness begins to spread horizontally across the horizon, this is the Second Fajr or True Fajr, and this is the onset of the time of the morning prayer and Fajr adhan. The end of the morning prayer time is sunrise.
citation_label: Islamic Law, Salah, Time of the morning prayer, p. 119

ruling_text: If the fasting individual travels in the afternoon, he is obliged to continue with his fast, but if he travels before noon, he is obliged to break his fast when he reaches hadd al-tarakhus, the limit of town. If one breaks his fast before reaching hadd al-tarakhus, then he is liable to kaffarah as an obligatory precaution.
citation_label: Islamic Law, Rulings of fasting for traveller, p. 259

question_text: What are examples of inherently najis things?
ruling_text: Najisat, or inherently najis things, include urine and faeces from every human being and from every haram-meat animal whose blood gushes out when slaughtered. Human semen is najis, and so too is that of an animal that has gushing blood when slaughtered. The carcass of an animal whose blood forcefully gushes out when slaughtered is najis, whether it died naturally or was slaughtered in a non-sharia way.
citation_label: Islamic Law, Taharah, Categories of najasat, p. 25
